crop.notes: The 'Chance Blows' item about Allen is complete at the top; the rest of the clipping is unrelated sporting notes (McAuliffe-Zeigler match, 'Dutch' Neil, the New Orleans syndicate). Top of the item sits at the foot of column 1 on the page and continues at the head of column 2.

ocr.notes: Allen's quote is mostly right; minor errors in the headline ("cf Bis Dstear") and scattered characters.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch printed Tom Allen's account of his defeat by Charley Gallagher: after winning the first round, he stepped into a snow-filled hole in the second and was knocked out by a blow to the neck.

metadata.notes: Masthead: Friday, St. Louis Post-Dispatch, October 26, 1894, page 7. Same item as article 901 (the headline deck of the 'Spring Race Meet' column).

facts.fact: Allen recalled that in his fight with Charley Gallagher he had the best of the first round, then stepped into a snow-filled hole in the second and was knocked out by a right to the big vein in the left side of his neck
facts.quote: The result was that a man whom I had bested in the first round put me out with a punch in the second.

notes: The printed text reads "I do say that it was a chance blow which defeated me, but it was through an accident..." (the sense suggests "I do not say"). The fight date is not given in the article; 1869 is the known Gallagher defeat and should be confirmed.
